classification.difficultyReason: The unsignposted version of this task (p14-q6-block) needs the student to set up the squared-distance equation, expand two binomials, simplify to a quadratic and factorise. Here that chain is split into three guided steps. (a) Write d² with the distance formula and expand two binomial squares, including the sign handling in (5−p)² and (p−2)². (b) Equate to 17 and reduce to a monic quadratic. (c) Factorise with product 6 and sum −7. The student makes no strategic choice and no square-root or check decision, and the PSF prompt supports the factorising. This is more demanding than p6-q4's single-step rearrangements. The algebra still chains several routine procedures, so it sits above those direct-application references but below the unscaffolded inverse-distance tasks.
